.. _multi-horizon:

Multiple investment periods
---------------------------

In general, there are two different methods of pathway optimisation with perfect
foresight. These differ in the way of accounting the investment costs:

* In the first case (type I), the complete overnight investment costs are applied.
* In the second case (type II), the investment costs are annualised over the years, in which an asset is active (depending on the build year and lifetime).

Type II is used in PyPSA since it allows a separation of the discounting over
different years and the end-of-horizon effects are smaller compared to method I.
For a more detailed comparison of the two methods and a reference to other energy
system models see `<https://nworbmot.org/energy/multihorizon.pdf>`_.

## Summary

I repaired two related bugs in the storage energy-balance constraints at `source/pypsa/optimization/constraints.py`, affecting both `define_storage_unit_constraints` and `define_store_constraints`.

**Root cause — the implausible boundary reset**

The supplied experiment uses `MultiIndex` snapshots but calls `n.optimize(...)` *without* `multi_investment_periods=True`. Every other multi-investment function in the codebase gates per-period logic on `n._multi_invest`, but the two storage functions gated only on `isinstance(sns, pd.MultiIndex)`. So the per-period block ran anyway and reset the store's energy to `e_initial` at the period boundary — producing the implausible `7.6 → 9.1` jump.

**Fix 1 — gating (the supplied experiment)**
Changed `if isinstance(sns, pd.MultiIndex):` to `if isinstance(sns, pd.MultiIndex) and n._multi_invest:` in both functions. Now a `MultiIndex` without multi-investment optimization is treated as one continuous timeline, consistent with the docs ("Multi-year investment … `n.optimize(multi_investment_periods=True)`").

**Fix 2 — per-period mask (generalization)**

The per-period boundary mask used `~e_cyclic` (overall cyclic) instead of `~e_cyclic_per_period`. For the default store (`e_cyclic=False`, `e_cyclic_per_period=True`), this incorrectly reset to `e_initial` at each period boundary instead of cycling within the period. Changed the mask to use `~e_cyclic_per_period` (and `~cyclic_state_of_charge_per_period` for `StorageUnit`). This makes "cyclic governs the boundary; the initial state is not its predecessor" hold when both per-period cyclic and initial-state conditions are set.

**Verification**
- `python reproduce.py` now reports continuous depletion: `7.6 → 6.7`, transition `-0.9`, terminal `5.3`.
- Conclusive multi-invest feasibility tests (both Store and StorageUnit): `e_cyclic_per_period=True` (incl. with `e_initial_per_period=True`) → cyclic governs, feasible even with `e_initial=0`; `e_initial_per_period=True` only → resets, correctly infeasible when empty; neither → continuous.
- Existing tests: no new failures. The only failures (MGA `LinearExpression contains nan`, stochastic `Kirchhoff-Voltage-Law` nan, `sklearn` missing, network-download errors) are all pre-existing on the untouched baseline.
